Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

heimdall 1.4.0

Breaking changes

  • update_state() now returns a list(obj =, drift =) for every detector, including the base drifter method and dfr_inactive(). Previously those returned the object itself, which broke the streaming loop shown in the examples.
  • dfr_kswin(), dfr_mcdd(), dfr_lbdd(), dfr_kldist() and dfr_aedd() gained a window_type argument. "sliding" (the new default) keeps at most window_size observations; "anchored" keeps every observation, pinning the reference half to the beginning of the stream. The 1.3.x behaviour of these four detectors corresponds to "anchored".
  • The dfr_aedd() values window_type = "fixed" and "moving" are deprecated aliases for "sliding" and "anchored". They still work and warn.
  • dfr_aedd() takes the autoencoder settings through ae_params (a named list forwarded to ae_class, plus error_function), gained the "psi" and "diff_threshold" criteria, and no longer has a reporting argument.
  • dfr_aedd() no longer accepts an autoencoder class that is neither an encoder nor an encoder-decoder; it fails with an explicit message instead of reaching an undefined variable.
  • dfr_kldist() is now multivariate: it consumes a data frame one row at a time, and every monitored column contributes to the score. Its target_feat argument now takes one or more column names (by default every numeric column), and it gained a breaks argument.
  • dfr_kldist(p_th) was renamed threshold, since it is not a p-value; p_th still works and warns. The default threshold is now 0.12, calibrated by simulation for the default window.
  • dfr_aedd() uses alpha only as the significance level of the hypothesis tests (it must now be between 0 and 1), and a new threshold argument for the "psi" and "diff_threshold" criteria, which compare the statistic directly.
  • stealthy() no longer has a monitored_features argument. Select the monitored columns with the target_feat of the drifter instead.
  • The drifter_output columns of dfr_mcdd() are now old_shapiro_p, new_shapiro_p and comparison_p, and the baselines dfr_inactive() and dfr_passive() report a drifter_output without columns.
  • dfr_mcdd() gained normality_alpha (default 0.05). The Shapiro-Wilk threshold no longer reuses alpha, which at its default of 1e-08 made the normality gate a no-op.
  • reset_state() on dfr_lbdd(), dfr_mcdd(), dfr_kldist() and dfr_aedd() restarts with an empty window (dfr_kswin() keeps its window). Together with the sliding policy, which tests as soon as the window is full (one observation earlier than 1.3.x), this moves the detection positions of dfr_kswin(), dfr_lbdd() and dfr_mcdd().
  • stealthy() gained back a reporting argument (default FALSE). The accumulation of drifter_input and drifter_output across every batch is now opt-in, since those frames grow with the whole stream.
  • fit() on a univariate detector now monitors only target_feat when it is given a data frame. It used to concatenate every column into a single stream. A data frame with several columns and no target_feat is now an error instead of being silently concatenated.
  • update_state() rejects ambiguous input instead of guessing: vectors with more than one value, text that is not a number, and, for error-based detectors, values other than 0, 1, TRUE or FALSE. Factors are read through their labels (previously through their internal codes), and infinite values are treated as missing, with a warning.
  • dfr_cusum() was reimplemented after MOA’s CusumDM, with the arguments lambda (now 50), delta and min_instances. The previous version added +1 per error and -1 per correct prediction, so it could only detect error rates above 50%.
  • dfr_multi_criteria() no longer keeps obj$drifts, which grew with every observation. Use obj$detections (alarms per detector) and obj$last_drifts (decisions on the last observation) instead. "and" now accepts detections up to fuzzy_window observations apart (it used to require them on the same observation, which almost never happens), and both "and" and "fuzzy" report a change once instead of on several consecutive observations. The "fuzzy" combination now costs the same per observation regardless of the length of the stream.
  • New defaults, calibrated by simulation to keep false alarms rare: dfr_kswin(window_size = 300, stat_size = 100, alpha = 1e-4, exact = NULL), dfr_lbdd(window_size = 300, alpha = 0.001), dfr_mcdd(window_size = 300, alpha = 1e-4), dfr_ecdd(average_run_length = 400) and dfr_aedd(monitoring_step = window_size / 2). The previous windows of 1500 observations were three times longer than the bundled example data.
  • dfr_aedd() now uses daltoolboxdp::autoenc_ed as its default autoencoder; the previous default no longer exists in daltoolbox.
  • st_drift_examples now holds six synthetic datasets (uv_virtual_drift, uv_vct_real_drift, uv_vdp_real_drift, mv_real_drift, mv_vct_real_drift and mv_vdp_real_drift). The former univariate and dataset1 are available as uv_virtual_drift and mv_real_drift.

New features

  • Every detector stores the per-observation diagnostics of its last fit() call in obj$drifter_output (for example the window width of ADWIN, the p-values of KSWIN and MCDD, or the divergence of dfr_kldist()), with one row per observation and NA where the detector reported nothing.
  • stealthy() always exposes the diagnostics of its drifter in obj$drifter_output, one row per row of x across every call to fit(), whatever the kind of drifter. reporting = TRUE now only controls the accumulation of the raw batches in drifter_input.
  • dfr_page_hinkley() gains direction = c("increase", "decrease", "both"). The default keeps the previous one-sided behaviour.
  • New dummy() ancestor class for the baseline detectors dfr_inactive() and dfr_passive().
  • mv_dist_based() takes a target_feat with one or more column names, so every distribution-based detector selects what it monitors the same way.
  • stealthy(history_size = ) bounds the rows kept in drifter_output and drifter_input, and nrm_memory(max_size = ) bounds the history used to estimate the normalization.
  • dfr_kswin() keeps its own random number stream, so it no longer changes the global random state while it runs, and gains a seed argument.
  • dfr_kldist() is about three times faster: the window is kept as a numeric matrix and the histograms are built with tabulate().

Bug fixes

Adaptive model

  • fit.stealthy() computed the error-based residuals against norm_x_oh, a variable that had been set to NULL a few lines earlier (or never defined). Every error-based detector received a null input. The batch is now projected once, through .stealthy_project_batch(), and used directly.
  • The drift check now runs before the model is updated, so error-based detectors observe prequential residuals instead of training error.
  • The detector is fed the incoming batch exactly once per call. The previous version fitted it with the new batch and then again with the whole accumulated x_train, and finally cleared drift_method$drifted, discarding the second signal.
  • predict.stealthy() with obsolete_model = "majority" referenced an undefined model variable and a norm_data_oh that had not been computed yet, and called an unimported cla_majority. obsolete_model is now validated with match.arg().
  • stealthy() initialised train_model only when class_balance = "buffer".
  • stealthy(target_uni_drifter = TRUE) works with factor targets; it used to feed NA to the detector, which then never detected anything.

Detectors

  • The sliding windows slide again. In 1.3.x dfr_kswin(), dfr_mcdd(), dfr_kldist() and dfr_lbdd() appended every observation without ever trimming, so memory grew without bound and the reference half stayed frozen on the first observations of the stream.
  • dfr_hddm() now detects increases of the error rate. A misplaced parenthesis in the bound that tracks the minimum error rate made the detector update that minimum on almost every observation, so it practically never reported a drift.
  • dfr_page_hinkley() compares sum - min_sum against the threshold again. 1.3.x compared sum alone, which is not the Page-Hinkley test, and left min_sum computed but unused.
  • dfr_page_hinkley() skips missing observations again. The tryCatch that replaced the NA guard let NA into the running mean and returned NULL from update_state() on any error, breaking the caller’s loop.
  • dfr_mcdd() applies exactly one comparison test per evaluation. 1.3.x fell through from the t-test to the Wilcoxon test, giving two uncorrected chances to reject.
  • dfr_kswin() requires both a significant p-value and a KS statistic above sqrt(-log(alpha) / stat_size), as in Raab et al., and subsamples its reference window again.
  • dfr_kswin() rejects window_size == stat_size, which crashed at the first test.
  • dfr_kldist() divided its score by the number of features plus one, because the temporary bin column was counted as a feature.
  • dfr_ecdd() used the last coefficient of the ARL 1000 polynomial (987.23) in the ARL 400 control limit; it now uses 848.18, as in the reference implementation.
  • dfr_ecdd() no longer fails with object 'control_limit' not found for average run lengths above 1000; the argument is validated up front.
  • dfr_cusum() and dfr_ecdd() restart after a drift, so they report each change once instead of on every following observation when reset_state() is not called.
  • dfr_aedd(), criterion parametric_threshold, compared the history mean against itself and could never fire.
  • dfr_aedd(), criterion psi, trimmed a non-existent state$window field.
  • dfr_aedd(), criterion levene, tested only the first reconstructed feature. It now tests every feature and combines the p-values with a Bonferroni correction.
  • dfr_aedd() no longer builds a throwaway autoencoder with input_size = 1 in the constructor, and no longer keeps its whole history in state$data under the sliding policy. It retrains the autoencoder when new columns appear, warns the first time it has to clip values outside [0, 1] and no longer fails on missing values.
  • dfr_aedd() and dfr_hddm() no longer latch the per-call drift flag. The drift element refers to the current call; obj$drifted stays sticky until reset_state().
  • fit.dfr_passive() iterated over 2:length(data), which is the column count for a data frame. All fit() methods now walk the stream through shared helpers.
  • fit() no longer breaks on a stream with a single observation, and rejects an empty one with a clear message.
  • Missing values are handled consistently: error-based detectors treat NA as a correct prediction, distribution-based detectors skip the observation.
  • Warm-start data (data =) longer than window_size is truncated to the most recent observations under the sliding policy; it used to make the window permanently longer.
  • dfr_multi_criteria() fails with a clear message when a detector’s target_feat is missing from the data, instead of never detecting.

Metrics and normalization

  • mt_fscore() uses its f argument as the beta of the F-beta score. It previously stored the parameter and always computed F1. The same formula was wrong in the twelve online-prediction example scripts, which have been fixed.
  • Precision, recall, F-score and accuracy accept factor and character labels. With a factor y_true, precision returned 1.5 and recall NaN. The metrics now also refuse vectors of different lengths instead of recycling them.
  • mt_rocauc() drops observations with missing scores, with a warning, instead of scoring them as zero.
  • inverse_transform.nrm_memory() inverts the data it is given instead of the internal history.
  • nrm_memory() no longer drops repeated rows from its history, which distorted the normalization (a z-score of 1.79 came out as 0.71).

Validation and documentation

  • Count parameters must be whole numbers, dfr_eddm() requires warning_level >= out_control_level, and target_feat must be a single column name.
  • nrm_base() objects keep the dal_base class.
  • The help pages state which changes each detector cannot see: DDM and HDDM only report increases of the error rate, LBDD only changes of spread, MCDD only changes of location.
  • ?st_drift_examples documents every bundled dataset.
  • dfr_adwin() is now implemented in pure R. It no longer needs reticulate, Python or numpy, and a dfr_adwin object can now be saved with saveRDS(). The port follows the scikit-multiflow implementation the previous version wrapped, so detections are expected to be the same.

Dependencies

  • caret and Metrics were dropped from Imports. One-hot encoding in stealthy() is now done internally with the same column names produced by caret::dummyVars(), and precision and recall are computed internally.
  • The bundled adwin.py module was removed: dfr_adwin() no longer needs Python. reticulate stays in Suggests only for the tests that check whether the Python backend of daltoolboxdp is available, and daltoolboxdp was added to Suggests for the default autoencoder of dfr_aedd().

Documentation and infrastructure

  • New vignettes: vignette("heimdall"), vignette("adaptive-models") and vignette("configuring-detectors").
  • Examples are organised in examples/1_detection and examples/2_online_prediction, with a detection example and an online prediction example for every drifter, including dfr_multi_criteria() and the dfr_inactive() and dfr_passive() baselines.
  • The README documents the output of each drifter, how each one selects its input, and which changes each one cannot see.
  • New tests cover every detector, stealthy(), dfr_multi_criteria(), the metrics and the internal helpers, plus statistical tests of the false-alarm rate and the detection delay of every detector across several seeds.
  • New GitHub Actions workflows for test coverage, linting (which now fails on any lint), R CMD check in the base image of the development container, the AEDD tests with the real autoencoder and the rendering of every example, and checks that reject file names invalid on Windows and committed merge conflict markers. A matching pre-commit hook is in .githooks/.
  • The code was restyled with styler, and legacy files, large raw datasets and orphaned example outputs were removed from the repository.
